skill.name: threat-modeling-expert
skill.description: Guides threat modeling with STRIDE, attack trees, architecture review, risk prioritization, mitigation planning, and security requirement extraction.
skill.summary: Guides structured threat modeling, risk prioritization, mitigation planning, and security requirement extraction.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited line is defensive guidance that warns against storing sensitive threat model details without access controls. It does not instruct system reconnaissance, collection, exfiltration, or unauthorized discovery.

content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss abuse paths, trust boundaries, and residual risks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured threat modeling and mitigation planning.
actual_capabilities: Defines system scope, assets, entry points, and trust boundaries.
Applies STRIDE analysis to components, data flows, and user interactions.
Builds attack trees for high-value workflows and critical failure paths.
Ranks threats by likelihood, impact, exposure, and business priority.
Maps mitigations to security controls, requirements, and residual risks.
Creates review-ready threat model documentation for architecture discussions.
limitations: Requires accurate architecture, data flow, and deployment context from the user.
Does not replace penetration testing, code review, or compliance certification.
Cannot verify controls without evidence from implementation, operations, or testing.
May need human security review for regulated or high-risk systems.

use_cases.title: Design New Architecture
use_cases.description: Identify threats before implementation by mapping data flows, trust boundaries, assets, and required controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Reviews
use_cases.description: Turn feature plans into prioritized threats, mitigations, and residual risk notes for review meetings.

use_cases.title: Improve Audit Readiness
use_cases.description: Document security assumptions, control mappings, and open risks before an internal or external assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me threat model this system. Ask me for scope, users, assets, data flows, trust boundaries, and deployment details before analysis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a new service

prompt_templates.title: Apply STRIDE
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply STRIDE to these components and data flows: [paste architecture]. List threats, affected assets, assumptions, and missing context.

prompt_templates.title: Build Attack Trees
prompt_templates.prompt: Build attack trees for these critical workflows: [paste workflows]. Include attacker goals, prerequisites, paths, mitigations, and residual risk.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this threat list and proposed mitigations. Rank risks, map controls, identify gaps, and produce security requirements for engineering.

output_examples.input: A team describes a payment API with external users, webhook callbacks, and admin access.
output_examples.output: A STRIDE threat summary covering spoofing, tampering, replay, authorization, logging, and rate limit recommendations.

output_examples.input: An architect shares data flows for a new document processing service.
output_examples.output: A prioritized list of threats, trust boundary concerns, required controls, and residual risk notes.

output_examples.input: A security lead provides critical workflows for account recovery.
output_examples.output: Attack tree narratives that show attacker goals, likely paths, mitigations, and remaining review questions.

best_practices: Bring current architecture diagrams, data flow details, and deployment assumptions into each session.
Record assumptions, owners, mitigations, due dates, and residual risks in the final model.
Update the threat model when components, data stores, trust boundaries, or access patterns change.
anti_patterns: Using threat modeling as a one-time checklist after implementation is complete.
Listing generic threats without tying them to assets, data flows, or controls.
Adding sensitive credentials, secrets, or customer data to shared threat model documents.

faq.question: Does this skill run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It guides structured analysis and documentation. Use scanners or testing tools for evidence from running systems.

faq.question: Which methodologies does it support?
faq.answer: It supports STRIDE, PASTA-style risk thinking, attack trees, control mapping, and security requirement extraction.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide architecture diagrams, data flows, trust boundaries, assets, user roles, deployment details, and known constraints.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and structure review work. High-risk systems still need qualified human security review.

faq.question: Can it help with existing systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze current architecture, identify missing controls, and document residual risks after changes.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive systems?
faq.answer: Use sanitized details when possible. Do not include secrets, customer records, or restricted incident data.
